items.title: Mississauga mayor-elect unveils transition team
items.summary: Just days after his sizeable victory, mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo has unveiled the list of people who have joined his transition team as he prepares to take over the role of mayor from Carolyn Parrish in November.

items.title: Mississauga Whistleblower Program to Add Fraud and Waste Hotline by Early 2027
items.summary: According to insauga.com, the City of Mississauga plans to launch an expanded Whistleblower Program in early 2027 that will let residents confidentially report suspected fraud, waste or wrongdoing at the municipality. The outlet reports a dedicated fraud and waste hotline is expected to be in place within the first three months of the year, giving both city employees and the public an independent and confidential way to raise concerns. According to a staff report cited by insauga.com, complaints will first be assessed by a team drawn from the internal audit, legal services and human resources departments, which will then decide whether to investigate internally or bring in an external investigator. The outlet says cases involving senior officials, such as the city manager or a commissioner, would likely be handed to an outside investigator to preserve independence. According to insauga.com, the city created its original Whistleblower Program in 2014, and internal audit director Amy Truong said in the staff report that it has supported accountability and ethical conduct for the past decade.

items.title: TikTok Video Spotlights Food World Plus's Chocolate and Snack Selection in Mississauga
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, the newly opened Food World Plus at 50 Matheson Blvd. is drawing shoppers in part for its extensive chocolate, candy and snack selection. The outlet reports the 176,000-square-foot multicultural grocery store stocks items from Europe, the Caribbean, the Middle East, East Asia and South Asia, along with a Costco-style warehouse section for bulk buying. Mississauga.com says the store also offers parking for 1,100 vehicles. The outlet quotes a TikTok user, @KirbyCub, who wrote that visiting the store changed their view of Mississauga as a tourist destination. According to mississauga.com, the store's size and variety have made it a draw for shoppers well beyond the immediate neighbourhood since it opened.

items.title: Credit Valley Conservation Nears Completion of First Watershed Plan Update Since 1956
items.summary: According to Credit Valley Conservation, the agency is in the final stages of a multi-year update to its Credit River Watershed plan, the first since the original document was created in 1956. CVC says the river runs roughly 90 kilometres from the northern Greater Toronto Area to its mouth in south Mississauga, and the plan covers the watershed across Mississauga, Brampton, Caledon and several other communities including Orangeville, Halton Hills and parts of Dufferin County. The agency reports the update draws on current science and data along with input from partners, stakeholders and the community to set long-term priorities for CVC and its municipal partners. According to CVC, a watershed plan serves as a tool for understanding the past and planning for the future health of the watershed. The agency says the new version is meant to guide its scope of work for years to come, reflecting decades of change across the region since the plan was first drafted nearly 70 years ago.

However, insurance costs in Mississauga are lower relative to the premiums in Brampton, the most expensive city in the region at $3,802 per year. 2% higher. items.title: Hazel McCallion Library Hosts Free Two-Day Comic and Gaming Expo Nov. 6-7
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the Mississauga Comic Expo returns to Hazel McCallion Central Library for a free two-day celebration of comics, gaming, art and fandom for all ages. The city says the event, hosted by Mississauga Library, includes workshops, panels, interactive activities, a cosplay red carpet and a green-screen photo booth. According to the city, attendees can browse the MCX Trading Post, learn to draw gag comics and chibi-style art, build miniatures, and try board games, video games and trivia contests. The city reports a Manga Lounge will let fans connect and browse manga, while families can take part in sketch challenges, Pokemon crafts, LEGO activities and a dance party. According to the city, Friday's program opens with activities followed by a superhero movie screening.

items.title: Canada-wide award recognizes community facility in Mississauga
items.summary: A Mississauga hockey and multi-purpose arena has won a national award for operating with energy efficiency in mind. The City of Mississauga said Paul Coffey Arena, named for the Mississauga native and Hockey Hall of Fame member, has been chosen Energy Star Building of the Year by Natural Resources Canada. ” That work at Paul Coffey Arena, they added, earned the facility the national recognition this week. “We are proud to receive this award because it recognizes the practical work our teams are doing to make city buildings more efficient and more affordable to operate,” said Anna Cascioli, City of Mississauga director of facilities and property management. “At Paul Coffey Arena, upgrades to lighting, building controls and arena equipment, supported by better performance data, are helping us use less energy and manage costs. ” Formerly called Malton Arena, the facility serves that community with Learn to Skate, ice hockey, public skating, ball hockey and other recreation programs, the city said.

items.title: Mississauga Shelter Opens Adoptions to Non-Residents During $25 Adopt-a-thon
items.summary: According to Mississauga Animal Services, dogs and cats at its shelter will be available for $25 plus tax and any applicable licence fees during an Adopt-a-thon running Nov. 2 to 14. The service reports the discounted rate is far below its regular fees of $280 for dogs and $190 for cats. According to an Oct. 29 news release, the event will run Monday through Saturday at the shelter, located at 735 Central Parkway. Mississauga Animal Services says the Adopt-a-thon is open to anyone, not just Mississauga residents, widening the pool of potential adopters. The service highlighted animals such as a dog named Messi among those currently available for adoption.

items.title: City Council's New Enforcement Rules Add $10 Charge When Parking Tickets Arrive by Mail
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga city council has approved a $10 fee that will apply whenever a parking infraction notice is delivered by mail instead of left on a vehicle's windshield. The outlet reports the charge took effect Oct. 1 alongside other changes to the city's parking enforcement rules, which now let bylaw officers record a licence plate and mail a notice to the registered owner when placing a ticket directly on the car would be unsafe or impractical. Insauga.com says enforcement officers will still affix tickets to windshields whenever it is safe to do so, and the mail option is meant as a fallback rather than a replacement. The outlet quotes Mississauga's community services commissioner, Raj Sheth, who told council that mailing a notice requires extra administrative work to prepare, process, print and send, which the new fee is meant to offset. According to insauga.com, the fee will be charged only in cases where a penalty notice is served by mail, not on tickets left on a windshield.

items.title: House of the week: Renovated bungalow with saltwater pool in Mississauga
items.summary: This place: A renovated bungalow in a sought-after Mississauga neighbourhood. Features: This renovated bungalow sits on a landscaped lot in coveted Lorne Park. The residence offers over 3,400 square feet of total interior space. The main level unfolds through an open-concept design with hardwood floors, pot lights and large windows in the living, dining and kitchen spaces. The kitchen anchors the home with direct views toward the backyard, a centre island and quartz countertops. The living room features a fireplace and a walkout. The primary bedroom offers a three-piece ensuite bathroom. Two additional bedrooms and a four-piece bathroom complete the main level. The basement features a recreation room, a second fireplace, two bedrooms, a three-piece bathroom, a laundry area and storage. An additional office/den provides a home workspace, games room, study or potential additional bedroom. A heated, saltwater, concrete pool is framed by landscaped grounds and patio space. The renovated cabana is complete with a television and an electronic roll-up door. A heated garage completes the package. Set within Lorne Park, the property offers access to schools, scenic walking trails, parks, recreational amenities, GO Transit, the QEW and Toronto Pearson Airport.

items.title: Mississauga’s energy-saving investments earn national recognition for Paul Coffey Arena
items.summary: ENERGY STAR® Building of the Year Award recognizes upgrades that lower energy use, reduce operating costs and support the City’s climate goals. Business and innovation | October 30, 2026 The City of Mississauga is investing in practical upgrades that help its buildings use less energy, cost less to operate and perform better over the long term. That work at Paul Coffey Arena has earned the facility the ENERGY STAR® Building of the Year Award from Natural Resources Canada. The arena serves the Malton community with Learn to Skate, ice hockey, public skating, ball hockey and other recreation programs. Behind the scenes, the City has made a number of improvements to help the facility use and track energy more efficiently, including: The award recognizes one facility, but the work is part of a broader City-wide approach to managing energy and costs. 5% compared to the 2023 baseline. Projects completed also secured approximately $195,000 in incentives. The improvements also help advance the Buildings and Clean Energy pathway in the City’s Climate Change Action Plan and support its targets to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 40 per cent by 2030 and 80 per cent by 2050, compared with 1990 levels. Natural Resources Canada’s ENERGY STAR Canada Awards recognize organizations and facilities that demonstrate leadership in energy efficiency. Paul Coffey Arena received the Building of the Year Award for its energy-saving upgrades and its ongoing use of ENERGY STAR® Portfolio Manager® to track performance and identify further improvements. Other ENERGY STAR-certified City facilities include Burnhamthorpe Library and Maja Prentice Theatre, Erin Mills Twin Arena, Mississauga City Hall, Ontario Court of Justice and Tomken Twin Arena.

items.title: A little less spooky, a lot safer: protect your home from CO
items.summary: Mississauga firefighters responded to 495 calls involving CO in homes last year. This November 1 to 7, make time to test your alarms and know the warning signs. Emergency and public safety | October 30, 2026 Once the pumpkins retire, give safety the spotlight. November 1 to 7 is Carbon Monoxide Awareness Week and Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services (MFES) is reminding residents to check their protection about a danger that stays out of site. Unlike Halloween’s make-believe scares, carbon monoxide (CO) poses a real risk. In 2025, MFES responded to 495 calls where CO was present in the home, up from 450 the year before. Knowing the risks, having working alarms and acting quickly can help keep you and your household safe. Known as the “silent killer,” CO is a harmful gas people can’t see, taste or smell. It is a poisonous gas produced when fuels such as natural gas, propane, gasoline, oil, and wood do not burn completely. Sources include fuel-burning appliances, fireplaces and vehicles running in attached garages. People and pets can be affected. You cannot see, smell or taste CO, so dangerous levels can build up unnoticed. Exposure can cause serious illness or death, and symptoms can be easy to mistake for something else. Working CO alarms provide an early warning so you can get outside and call for help.
